source_text: What the heck? 4 minutes per record? Can't they be batched?
reply_text:
㊥ Gist: Yes, they can be batched. The time goes on tool calls, about 67 per turn, not on judgement, so I have dispatched a builder that fetches everything in advance and lets a reader do ten turns in one pass.

🈖 (where the four minutes go) For each fragment the reader runs two pattern searches, then opens each plausible pattern file to read its IF and THEN, then fills a template, validates and publishes. Each of those steps is a separate round trip to the model. Codex's one record took 67 tool calls. The other readers were faster per record, 1.2 to 1.5 minutes, but by the same method.

㊭ (the batched version: `scripts/backfill_pack.py`, zai-1)
- **`pack`** builds one file for ten turns. It holds:
  - each turn's text with sentence ids and offsets, plus the two previous turns of the same session as context;
  - move hits and subject hits for every sentence, with every pattern of a family the turn names;
  - an appendix giving each distinct pattern's conclusion, context, IF, HOWEVER and THEN once.
- The reader reads that one file and returns one JSON array covering all ten turns, with no tool calls. If nothing in the pack fits a turn, it can name up to three extra searches for a second round.
- **`publish`** validates and publishes each turn separately through the existing validator. A bad turn is refused on its own and the rest still publish. Nothing is ever overwritten.
- Job: `invoke-1790789698242-29257-4d26bd96`
- Park: `park-878c58ef-71ce-4a2c-903f-0624b935ccb4`

㊟ (what batching trades away) A reader can only judge the patterns the search surfaced, which is why the pack carries subject hits and whole named families as well as move hits. The "no generator scripts" rule stays. It was there to stop a reader writing analyses by program without reading, and here the reader still writes every analysis itself.

㊢ (next) When the builder lands I will check it and build the pack for chunk 4. That pack goes to one reader as a single job, and I will time it against the 1.2 to 4 minutes a record we have now. I expect about ten turns in a few minutes, but that is a guess until it runs.

previous_reply_acts.text: Gist: Agreed, it probably can. To find out rather than guess, I have given Codex sol the same ten turns Sonnet read, as an independent second reading.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text: (why the first result is not a fair comparison) Codex read different turns from Sonnet, and shorter ones: 7 to 58 words against Sonnet's 9 to 81. Its coarser cutting may come partly from the turns and partly from the packet. The packet said nothing about cutting one sentence into several moves, and Sonnet did that without being told. The early stop came from the packet too: it offered "leave it requested" as an acceptable outcome.

previous_reply_acts.author: claude-17
previous_reply_acts.text:
(the test) codex-9 is rereading chunk 2's ten turns in a separate directory, `storage/operator-turns/rereads/chunk2-codex9/`. That keeps the second reading out of the pattern graph and out of 小象's training counts. The packet now says to cut by move, with one fragment per move even inside a sentence. It also tells the reader not to look at the other reading.
- Job: `invoke-1790789293370-29253-7af6911b`
- Park: `park-7305f4d2-5718-4421-bc6b-22619fd85c03`, 55-minute deadline
